In 25 years, India has flipped the script on Defence Production.

We went from buying 70% of our security to building 75% of it.

The infographic below isn’t just a curve; it’s the timeline of India’s strategic autonomy.

Here’s the breakdown of the shift.👇

The Starting Line (2000):

Post-Kargil war, the reality was harsh.

• Import Dependency: ~70%

• Domestic Share: ~30%

• The Ecosystem: 100% State-run (OFBs/DPSUs).

We were the world’s largest open chequebook for arms dealers. 

The private sector was virtually locked out.

The "Lost Decade" & The Pivot (2005–2014)

Policy paralysis slowed the climb.

Despite opening the sector to private players in 2001, we saw "frameworks" but no factories.

Imports soared as we replaced vintage Soviet gear with modern Western platforms - off - the -shelf. 

The indigenisation needle barely moved past 40%.

The Catalyst (2015–2020)

Three moves changed the trajectory:

"Make in India" (2014): 

Prioritized Indian-designed gear (IDDM).

The "Negative" Lists (2020): We banned the import of 5,000+ items (artillery, light tanks, comms). 

If we could make it, we had to buy it local.

FDI Liberalisation: 74% allowed under automatic route.

The New Reality (2025)

The curve hits escape velocity.

• Capital Budget for Indian Industry: 75% (Record High)

• Production Value: >₹1.5 Lakh Cr

• Exports: ₹23,000+ Cr (Armenia, Philippines, etc.)

We aren't just making small 
parts anymore; we are making the platforms (LCH, Tejas, C-295).

The Takeaway

It took 25 years to invert the ratio.

• 2000: 70% Imported / 30% Made

• 2025: 25% Imported / 75% Made

This isn't just about saving forex; it's about supply chain resilience. 

In a crisis, you can't fight with an invoice. You need the factory.

What's Next?

The challenge shifts from "Can we make it?" to "Can we design it?"

The next 5 years will be defined by R&D ownership, aero-engines, and bringing the 75% to 90%.

data.raw_text:
I’ll be fully transparent.

2025 was a year of wins, but also failures.

Here’s a clear breakdown of what happened and where I’m headed in 2026. Public accountability.

First, the wins.

PERSONAL

 • Traveled across Thailand and Vietnam for 6 months

 • Met incredible people along the way

 • Solid gym progress (78kg lean at some point this year)

 • Read 60+ books and summaries (mostly via Shortform)

BUSINESS

 • Scaled Notionbase with a new website, blog, products, and freebies

 • Grew the YouTube channel to 10k+ subscribers

 • Made $4k in my first year selling digital products (Gumroad + Notion Marketplace)

 • Crossed my first $1k/month milestone

 • Went from 0 to 1,000 followers on X

Now, the losses.

PERSONAL

 • A life-threatening injury in Vietnam
 → Lost 10kg during the months following surgery
 → Took a real mental hit
 → Had to fly back home for insurance and treatment

 • Too much scrolling and YouTube (guilty)

 • Poor sleep habits

 • Inconsistent meditation and breathwork

BUSINESS

 • Spent too much time building great products and not enough time marketing them (a.k.a. what moves the money needle)

 • Didn’t post as much content and products as planned

 • Experimented with algorithmic trading, which led to emotional ups and downs (I lost more than I made). I realized I wasn’t aligned with it and eventually stopped.

Still, this year gave me something more valuable than growth.

Clarity.

I’m clearer than ever on what I want to build and why.

I realized I don’t want to tie my entire identity to a single tool like Notion (even though I genuinely love it).

And I also don’t want to become another loud “motivational trader” guru chasing attention.

My mission is simple: help solopreneurs organize their life and business, make more money, and live a more free and aligned life.

And most importantly, I want to practice what I preach.

So here’s what’s next.

PERSONAL

 • Going back to working while traveling and intentionally networking (I'm actually flying to the Philippines in 5 days, I'll keep you posted on that).

 • After the longest break I’ve taken in 9 years (6 months), I’m committing again to a serious gym and health routine. Fitness has always been my anchor and my gateway to discipline in both life and business, and I really missed it in the second half of the year.

BUSINESS

 • Clear separation between my Notion content (Notionbase) and my personal brand as a solopreneur (William Coste)

 • Doubling down on my personal brand through:
 – X content
 – A biweekly newsletter (Solopreneur Stories, just launched)
 – A weekly podcast (Solopreneurship, coming soon)

 • Long-term goal: build a complete digital products ecosystem: courses, Notion templates, and systems for solopreneurs.

That’s my plan for 2026.

What’s yours?

P.S. Just launched my personal website, all links in bio.

 P.P.S. Follow me on X, bookmark this post for updates, and join the newsletter for weekly, honest lessons on solopreneurship, systems, and freedom.
→ https://t.co/ABl4wXl7SG
